meta.title: Ondra Failure Attribution
meta.description: Eight-class failure attribution with a wound ledger (handbook §8.6, P1). The handbook's own words: Ondra currently has only silent degradation, no attribution — and the cost of silent degradation is not ugliness but the inability to learn: the same mistake a hundred times, swallowed each time, still unexplained the next. On every tool call, a failure is sorted into exactly one of tool_missing, arg_error, permission, timeout, network, not_found, conflict or unknown, opening a wound; the wound closes only when that same tool next succeeds, and is marked chronic after five minutes, at which point retrying stops and a human is waited for. Three judgements are hard-wired. First, arg_error never auto-retries — it is not in the prescription table but on the first line of the retry-budget function, so editing the table cannot remove it; the handbook's reason is that retrying a hundred times will not get someone who does not know the password logged in. Second, a wound closes only on that tool's own next success, not on a timeout and not because some other tool worked, because closing on time makes a permanently broken tool look healed. Third, the five-minute chronic threshold is verbatim. Of the eight prescriptions only timeout and network point at trying again; the other six point at supplying what is missing, since agent mistakes are structural — a gap in what the agent knows, not a bug. This package is also the single wiring point between the upstream tool-result event and the organ ABI: it converts every result into a read-only view and feeds the organ host, without which no organ's onToolResult would ever fire. It never rewrites tool results, never adds a tool, installs no timers and writes nothing to disk.
